chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a group of thieves against whom the evidence had been established and who had confessed. He said: so he cut off their hands, then he said: “O Qanbar, take them to yourself, treat their wounds, and care for them well. Then when they recover, inform me.”

When they recovered, he came to him and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the people upon whom you carried out the prescribed punishments have recovered from their wounds.” He said: “Go and clothe each man among them with two garments and bring them to me.” He said: so he clothed each of them with two garments and brought them to him in the best appearance, wrapped and covered, as though they were a people in iḥrām. They stood before him, and he turned toward the ground, tracing it with his finger for a long while, then he raised his head toward them and said: “Uncover your hands.”

Then he said: “Raise [your hands] to the sky and say: O Allah, indeed ʿAlī has cut us.” So they did so, and he said: “O Allah, it is upon Your Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.”

Then he said to them: “O these people, if you repent, you will receive your hands back, and if you do not repent, you will be joined to them.” Then he said: “O Qanbar, let them go on their way, and give each one of them what suffices him until his town.”

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: clear legal proof or evidence establishing the offense
key_terms.الْحُدُودَ: the prescribed legal punishments set by the sacred law
key_terms.تُبْتُمْ: you repented and turned back to Allah
key_terms.خَلِّ سَبِيلَهُمْ: let them go on their way
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as legal and religious authority
key_terms.فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ: he carried out the prescribed amputation of their hands
key_terms.كِتَابِكَ: Your Book, meaning the Qur'an as the basis of judgment

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام implement the punishment for theft with justice and compassion?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام carried out the legal punishment for theft after proof and confession were established. It also shows his care for the punished men afterward through treatment, clothing, exhortation to tawbah (repentance), and provision for their return, joining legal enforcement with mercy and moral reform.
